structural_tricks_not_yet_tried_summary: T1 (proof route) Multivariable adelic capacity theory (Chinburg-Hemenway Falk-Heninger-Scherr) applied to the S_5 congruence: would convert the W10 1/32 ceiling, which covers only full-rank triangular (p,f)^ell lattices, into a theorem over ALL auxiliary-polynomial methods (including unravelled linearisation and sublattices), or exhibit the alternative-(1) regime where a finite zero locus exists. Toy falsifier: S_3 (bivariate, degree 2), compute the capacity threshold in delta and compare with the measured reach 1/6 and the ceiling 1/4.

T2 (tool route) Ehrhart/DimOracle (2026/244) pricing of an unravelled-linearisation lattice for S_5: this is exactly the W10 §7 class with no ceiling. Honest expectation: unravelled linearisation historically moves the exponent by at most ~0.01 (Boneh-Durfee 0.284 -> 0.292) or halves dimension at fixed exponent (2026/2109); no substitution u=g(x) with |u| smaller than its monomials is visible in S_5 because the internal addition-tree nodes have full size p. Falsifier: run cuso/DimOracle on S_3 with u = x1 x2 substitutions and check the reach stays <= 1/4.

T3 (binary-curve route) Function-field Coppersmith (Cohn-Heninger 2010/2013) on F_2[t]: the Weil-descent factor base {deg_t x < ell} IS the small-root set, lattice reduction over F_q[t] is exact and polynomial-time, and the univariate theorem is rigorous (deg w < beta^2 n/d). delta-reach for S_{m+1} in units ell/n: JM-box 1/(m(m+1)2^{m-2}) (1/24 at m=3, 1/80 at m=4), ceiling 1/(m 2^{m-1}) (1/12, 1/32) versus the needed ell/n ~ 1/m (1/3, 1/4). Same wall as F_p, but rigorous and with exact reduction; worth a toy run only as a *rigorous lower-bound certificate* for the lattice substitute for Gröbner descent. novelty_unverified: no literature found combining function-field Coppersmith with summation polynomials.

T4 (hybrid pattern) Lattice-supplies-one-relation + BSGS-finishes (Gao-Feng-Hu-Pan rank-3 lattice, second reduced vector): for ECDLP every such hybrid sits under the generic oracle bound S T^2 >~ r/|Aut| unless the lattice step uses the field representation; it does (small x), so the pattern is admissible in principle but the lattice step is still S_5 at reach <= 1/32.

T5 (multi-equation accounting) The 'number of equations as a parameter' symbolic polytope volume of 2025/2044 is the right instrument for the unexamined W10 class 'joint lattice for the three-block (4,2) S_3-tree system' (three equations in six unknowns, two of them internal nodes). Obstruction to expect: internal-node unknowns have size p, so every monomial containing them already exceeds the modulus; eliminating them returns S_5.

papers.title: Provable Lattice Reduction in Nearly the Time of QR Factorization
papers.authors: Yang Zhou, Zhedong Wang, Mingsheng Wang
papers.summary: Deterministic lattice reduction with bit complexity Õ(n^ω (1 + log κ_col(B))), i.e. QR-factorisation time up to logs, with no heuristic assumptions (iterative precision management, finer potential, new basis/transform representation inside a recursive framework). Implementation beats flatter in instruction count on all 153 benchmark executions (median ratios 1.55 q-ary, 1.86 NTRU-like; Coppersmith inputs included). Code availability not stated on the abstract page.
papers.relevance: Engineering lever for the lattice stage only. S_5 delta-reach: unchanged (1/80 box, ceiling 1/32); faster reduction lets the ell=2 S_5 lattice (dimension 729, reach delta_2 = 0.0144) be run where the repo's BigInt LLL could not, but ell=3 (dimension ~2.3M at L=38) stays out of reach and no multiplicity reaches 1/5. Classification: engineering.
papers.suggested_route: Use as the reduction engine if any S_5 lattice probe at ell=2 is ever run as a finite-p control; not a research lever.

papers.title: Bounds on polynomial approximations of the discrete logarithm function
papers.authors: Swastik Kopparty, Rishabh Kothary, Ashutosh Shankar
papers.summary: Sharpens Coppersmith-Shparlinski 2000: a degree-D polynomial over F_p agrees with dlog on at most (1+o(1))sqrt(Dp) points (Johnson-bound/list-decoding proof, nontrivial even for D > p/2); for D=1 the agreement count is O(p^{2/5}) via sum-product estimates; improved bounds on how many points (x, dlog x) a bivariate Q(X,Y) of degree <= D can vanish on. Stated for F_p^*, not E(F_p). Full PDF not accessible (403); abstract via arXiv.
papers.relevance: Cross-lane obstruction (brief §3 levers 8 and 12): any 'x-functional filter' or learned predictor that is a low-degree polynomial in the field representation agrees with the logarithm on O(sqrt(Dp)) inputs, i.e. a vanishing fraction; the bivariate statement kills low-degree algebraic relations between x and log. Not yet transferred to E(F_p) (would need the elliptic analogue of the Johnson-bound argument). No S_5 delta-reach (not a small-root method).
papers.suggested_route: Toy falsifier for lever 8/12: on random curves at p ~ 2^16-2^20, fit degree-D polynomials in x(P) to log_G(P) (least squares over F_p via interpolation on random subsets) and count agreements; compare to sqrt(Dp). Proof route: adapt the list-decoding argument to the elliptic 'code' {(x(P), log P)}.

papers.title: Attacking CRT-RSA with Small Exponents via Unravelled Linearization
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Ding, Yanshuo Zhang, Zhaopeng Dai, Ziyang Yan, Ying Chen
papers.summary: Unravelled-linearisation Coppersmith lattice for balanced CRT-RSA with small d_p, d_q: same asymptotic bound as Takayasu-Lu-Peng (d_p,d_q < N^0.122) but lattices of about half the dimension and theory matching experiment; extensions to MSB-leakage models by variable substitution.
papers.relevance: Calibration datum for W10 open class 1: in the most-studied setting, unravelled linearisation halved dimension and left the exponent unchanged. For S_5 this predicts constant-factor dimension savings, not movement from 1/80 toward 1/5. No S_5 delta-reach change expected; classification: engineering.
papers.suggested_route: None beyond citing it when pricing T2.

papers.title: Computing Asymptotic Bounds for the Automated Coppersmith Method via Linear Programming
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Ding, Zhaopeng Dai, Baofeng Wu, Yanshuo Zhang, Kejun Zhang
papers.summary: Converts the asymptotic-bound computation of the Meers-Nowakowski automated Coppersmith method into a linear program with a provably correct explicit formula; improved bounds for CI-HNP, MIHNP, EC-HNP, LCG with unknown multiplier, and the leveled isogeny problem with hints (POKE). Handles systems with different modulus powers; examples eliminate hidden variables by Gröbner basis before the LP. A search snippet of the PDF states that a single modular congruence of total degree d does not appear to yield a symmetric small-root bound beyond M^{1/d} (unverified: PDF 403).
papers.relevance: Already the programme's W10 reference (KN-LIT-1599); W10 built its own closure LP from the abstract. For S_5 (total degree 32) the quoted remark is consistent with the W10 charging ceiling 1/32 per variable. The hidden-variable elimination step is the formal reason the S_3-tree multi-polynomial route collapses to S_5.
papers.suggested_route: If the PDF becomes accessible, check whether its LP admits non-convex monomial sets; if yes, run it on S_4 to test the 1/21.8 convex bound.

papers.title: New Asymptotic Results on Predicting Polynomial Congruential Generators
papers.authors: Yansong Feng, Abderrahmane Nitaj, Yanbin Pan, Mengce Zheng
papers.summary: Coppersmith attacks on polynomial congruential generators from arbitrarily many truncated outputs; the success condition is expressed as the volume of a high-dimensional Newton-type polytope computed SYMBOLICALLY as a function of the number of equations (extending the Feng et al. CRYPTO 2025 sumset framework). Improved bounds for Pollard and linear generators; new attacks on quadratic generators with partially known coefficients and perturbed power generators.
papers.relevance: First automated machinery where the number of modular equations is a free parameter. That is the instrument for the W10 unexamined class 'joint multi-polynomial lattices' (three S_3 blocks in six unknowns, or several targets). Expected S_5 outcome: internal-node unknowns have size p, every monomial containing them exceeds the modulus, elimination returns S_5, so no reach gain; but the computation has never been done and is cheap.
papers.suggested_route: T5: write the (4,2) S_3-tree system {S_3(x1,x2,u), S_3(x3,x4,v), S_3(u,v,z)} with |x_i|<p^delta, |u|,|v|<p, and compute the symbolic polytope-volume condition as a function of multiplicity; report the resulting delta and compare with 1/80.

papers.title: Efficient Polynomial System Solving via Dixon Resultants: Applications to AO Primitives
papers.authors: Haohai Suo, Jiamin Cui
papers.summary: Revisits the Dixon resultant for simultaneous multi-variable elimination; refined Dixon-matrix size bounds via lattice-path counting; open-source C solver DRSolve, competitive with Magma/msolve on random well-determined systems and better in the low-variable / high-degree regime; three elimination strategies for underdetermined parametric systems.
papers.relevance: Cross-lane (algebraic root finding, brief §3 lever 2), not small roots: S_4/S_5 membership over F_p is exactly a low-variable / high-degree system (4 unknowns, degree 8). DRSolve is a new all-roots engine to price against msolve/Macaulay in the d4_symmetrised_s5 pipeline. Does not touch the lattice delta-reach.
papers.suggested_route: Benchmark DRSolve against msolve on the D4-invariant S_5 Weil system (4,200 columns) at p = 29..269; a constant-factor result at best (engineering).

papers.title: Revisit Unravelled Linearization with Ehrhart (quasi-)Polynomial
papers.authors: Yansong Feng, Yiming Gao, Honggang Hu, Abderrahmane Nitaj, Yanbin Pan, Mengce Zheng
papers.summary: Shows that the standard interpolation-based asymptotic analysis of unravelled-linearisation lattices (Herrmann-May 2009, and the cuso tool) can be wrong because lattice dimension/determinant are Ehrhart QUASI-polynomials in the multiplicity, or polynomial only above a threshold; derives bounds rigorously via Ehrhart theory and Barvinok's algorithm (volumes of faces of the Newton polytope). Improves LCG, quadratic generator, subset-sum generator and POKE partial-key attacks (POKE MSB leakage 85.29% -> 79.81%). DimOracle predicts the required lattice dimension.
papers.relevance: Directly the W10 §7 class 1 (non-full-rank / unravelled lattices) for which the programme has no ceiling and no tool. It also warns that the programme's own ell->infinity extrapolations for S_4/S_5 (box family closed form) are safe only because the box family is a genuine polynomial case. S_5 delta-reach: not computed by this paper; expectation from T2 is <= 1/32.
papers.suggested_route: T2: build the Ehrhart counting for S_3 with candidate linearisations (u = x1 x2, u = x1 + x2) and for the elementary-symmetric encoding; verify the exact closure numbers of W10 (1/18, 1/10, 0.119 at ell=1,2,3) and then price S_4 at ell=2..4 where W10 could not reach.

papers.title: Coppersmith's Method for Solving Modular Inversion Hidden Number Problem via Determinant-Based Elimination
papers.authors: Zhaopeng Ding, Zhaopeng Dai, Baofeng Wu, Rundong Wang, Yanshuo Zhang
papers.summary: New determinant-based strategy for generating shift polynomials (a search snippet describes it as the first use of algebraically DEPENDENT polynomials in a Coppersmith lattice); beats prior MIHNP and ICG bounds in theory and experiment; shows MIDHNP is no harder than MIHNP, disproving a Boneh et al. 2001 conjecture. PDF not accessible; details unverified.
papers.relevance: Already cited by W10. Structural trick: shift polynomials that are determinants of systems sharing a hidden variable, i.e. elimination performed INSIDE the lattice instead of by resultant beforehand. For S_5 the analogous move (eliminate the internal node u between S_3(x1,x2,u) and S_3(x3,x4,u) inside the lattice) is the only unexamined way to avoid paying the full degree-8 Newton box; whether it beats the box is exactly W10 §7 class 2/3.
papers.suggested_route: Once the PDF is readable, instantiate the determinant construction on S_3 x S_3 -> S_4 and compare its determinant exponent with the box 1/24.

papers.title: On Factoring and Power Divisor Problems via Rank-3 Lattices and the Second Vector
papers.authors: Yiming Gao, Yansong Feng, Honggang Hu, Yanbin Pan
papers.venue: IACR ePrint 2025/1004; arXiv 2512.19076 (math.NT); listed as major revision for Math. Comp.
papers.summary: Deterministic factoring via a rank-3 Coppersmith lattice combined with baby-step giant-step; uses the SECOND LLL-reduced vector (the shortest is a trivial (j, mX, 0) vector that forces a trivial collision). Balanced semiprimes in O(N^{1/5} log^{13/5} N / (log log N)^{3/5}); a^n ± b^n in O(N^{1/5} log^{13/5} N) (from N^{1/4}); r-power divisors O(r^{1/4} N^{1/4r} log^{5/2} N) in the worst case N = p^r q.
papers.relevance: A lattice + generic-collision hybrid in which the lattice supplies a quadratic relation and BSGS finishes; the structural novelties (rank-3 lattice, second vector to dodge trivial solutions) are generic Coppersmith tricks. For ECDLP any such hybrid is bounded by S T^2 >~ r/|Aut| unless the lattice step uses the field representation; the relevant lattice step is S_5 with reach <= 1/32, so no change. Pattern worth remembering: trivial short vectors (e.g. the negation/symmetry vectors in a symmetrised S_5 lattice) should be excluded by taking later reduced vectors rather than by shrinking the box.
papers.suggested_route: Check whether the W10 finite-p S_3 lattices (dim 9/25) had their 'first m rows' test defeated by symmetry-induced trivial short vectors; re-score using the first m NON-trivial rows.

papers.title: Better Bounds for Finding Fixed-Degree Isogenies via Coppersmith's Method
papers.authors: Marius A. Aardal, Diego F. Aranha, Yansong Feng, Yiming Gao, Yanbin Pan
papers.summary: Finds degree-d isogenies between supersingular curves over F_{p^2} via small roots of a FOUR-variable INTEGER equation, adapting the explicit sumset asymptotic formulas of Feng et al. (CRYPTO 2025) from the modular to the integer setting; classical Õ(max{p^{1/2}, exp(O(log^{4/5} p)) d/p^{2/3}}) vs Benčina et al. d/p^{5/8}; quantum analogue; fixes an omitted sub-exponential factor in Benčina et al.
papers.relevance: The one recent place where multivariate Coppersmith enters an elliptic-curve structural problem; the equation is an integer (not mod-p) relation with four unknowns, and the gain came from the sumset formula, not from a new lattice shape. For S_5 (modular, dense box) the same formulas give the 1/80 already in the atlas.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: A note on the analysis of Herrmann-May lattices for small exponent RSA
papers.authors: Abul Kalam, Sudeshna Karmakar, Santanu Sarkar
papers.summary: Finds a 15-year-old error in the Herrmann-May (PKC 2010) unravelled-linearisation asymptotics (floor(m/t) j approximated by (m/t) j): the corrected bound is d < N^0.292256, strictly below Boneh-Durfee's 1 - 1/sqrt2. A refined construction that drops low-index y-shifts (threshold ~(sqrt2+1) j, basis stays triangular) reaches the Boneh-Durfee bound with far smaller dimension (276,760 -> 21,353 at delta = 0.292).
papers.relevance: Second warning (with 2026/244) that unravelled-linearisation asymptotics are fragile; the dimension savings are the realistic yield of shift-selection tricks (constant factors). No S_5 reach change.
papers.suggested_route: None beyond methodological caution for T2.

papers.title: Computing Asymptotic Bounds for Small Roots in Coppersmith's Method via Sumset Theory
papers.authors: Yansong Feng, Hengyi Luo, Qiyuan Chen, Abderrahmane Nitaj, Yanbin Pan
papers.summary: First provable algorithm for the asymptotic bounds of Jochemsz-May basic and extended strategies (single polynomial and systems), via sumsets of Newton polytopes; open-source; improved CI-HNP bounds over CSURF.
papers.relevance: The programme's reach calculator is calibrated to this framework and its (n! vol Newt)^{-1/n} bound (1/70.8 for S_5) is the convex-set consequence. Already in the lead card LEAD-ICP-coppersmith-smallroot-semaev.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Solving Multivariate Coppersmith Problems with Known Moduli (cuso)
papers.authors: Keegan Ryan
papers.summary: Gröbner-basis algorithm that provably computes an optimal shift-polynomial set for a given monomial set (lattice provably contains all desired short vectors; often large rank), a graph-optimisation heuristic for low-rank alternatives, and polytope-based automatic asymptotic bounds; matches or improves a dozen prior attacks. cuso needs Sage + flatter + msolve.
papers.relevance: Already the W10 and 2026-10-26 reference; the programme proved that on convex monomial sets Ryan-optimal shifts cannot beat 1/70.8 for S_5. Open only on non-convex monomial sets (W10 §7 class 2). Sage hangs in this sandbox, so cuso cannot be run here.
papers.suggested_route: Non-convex M test on S_3 outside the sandbox (cuso), as the cheapest probe of class 2.

papers.title: Solving ECDLP over F_p with Pre-computation via Representation Technique
papers.authors: Claire Delaplace, Pierre-Alain Fouque, Paul Kirchner, Alexander May
papers.summary: UNVERIFIED (HAL blocked; abstract from search snippets): extends Delaplace-May's F_{p^2} representation-technique attack to prime fields with precomputation: p^{4/5} online time after a p^{6/5} precomputation over F_p, and p^{2/(2l+1)} online after p^{(l+1)/(2l+1)} precomputation over F_{p^l}; the authors state it does not beat Bernstein-Lange precomputation.
papers.relevance: The only representation-technique (Howgrave-Graham-Joux lineage) result on prime-field ECDLP after Delaplace-May 2019. S T^2 = p^{6/5} (p^{4/5})^2 = p^{14/5} >> p, so it sits far above the Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan line; consistent with the brief's Wagner/k-list closure (no small visible quotient). Out of the 2023-2026 window but missing from the atlas (only Delaplace-May 2019, KN-LIT-ae78e5, is there).
papers.suggested_route: Record in the atlas as closed_known under the k-list wall; no experiment.

papers.title: Subset Balancing and Generalized Subset Sum via Lattices
papers.authors: Yiming Gao, Yansong Feng, Honggang Hu, Yanbin Pan
papers.summary: Lagarias-Odlyzko-style reductions of Subset Balancing / Generalized Subset Sum with coefficient set {-d..d} to a single SVP_infty or CVP_infty instance in dimension n+1; deterministic Õ((6 sqrt(2 pi e))^n) and randomised Õ(2^{2.443 n}) beating meet-in-the-middle for d >= 15; polynomial time for large d; extension to any centrally symmetric convex body; worst-case 2^{O(n log log d)} and average-case Õ((18 sqrt(2 pi e))^n) for generalized subset sum.
papers.relevance: Lagarias-Odlyzko lane item. Not applicable to E(F_p) relation collection: these reductions need a Z-linear embedding of the target group (integers, or F_q[t]); a prime-order E(F_p) has no non-trivial homomorphism to Z or to a small quotient, which is the brief's Wagner/k-list wall restated. No S_5 reach.
papers.suggested_route: None (obstruction named: no abelian-group-to-Z embedding; Tate/prime order).

papers.title: Upper bounds for failure probabilities of reductions from low density subset sum problems to lattice problems on linearly independent vectors
papers.authors: Shoichi Kamada
papers.summary: Introduces l-SIVP (SVP at l=1, SIVP at l=rank) and bounds, via Ehrhart theory, the failure probability of Lagarias-Odlyzko / Coster-et-al. reductions from low-density subset sum; tighter than Coster et al. at l=1.
papers.relevance: Same inapplicability as the previous entry (no Z-embedding of E(F_p)). Noted because Ehrhart counting is now the common language of both the LO-density and the Coppersmith-dimension analyses (2026/244), which could unify the programme's two lattice calculators.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Beating Meet-in-the-Middle for Subset Balancing Problems
papers.authors: Tim Randolph, Karol Węgrzycki
papers.summary: First WORST-CASE improvement over the |C|^{n/2} meet-in-the-middle barrier for Subset Balancing with C = {-d..d}, d>1 (and C\{0}, d>2), by extending the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique to adversarial inputs (mixing for worst-case inputs, flexible representations without 0, recovering solution pairs from pseudo-solution pairs); exponential improvement for Equal Subset Sum.
papers.relevance: Representation-technique lane item. Still requires modular filtering of partial sums (a quotient of the ambient group), which E(F_p) of prime order lacks; the Delaplace-May route around this (polynomial multi-evaluation) is the one already in the atlas and is p^{1.314}. No S_5 reach.
papers.suggested_route: None (obstruction: no visible quotient for filtering).

papers.title: Lattices in function fields and applications
papers.authors: Christian Bagshaw, Bryce Kerr
papers.summary: Extends Mahler's function-field geometry of numbers to bound intersections of lattices with convex bodies in F_q((1/T))^d, more precisely than the real analogues; applications: counting solutions of congruences in F_q[T] with variables in short intervals, and counting points on polynomial curves lying in LOW-DIMENSIONAL SUBSPACES of finite fields (improving Bagshaw, Cilleruelo-Shparlinski-Zumalacárregui); unified energy/point-count framework.
papers.relevance: Cross-lane number theory for the binary-curve factor base: 'points of a curve in a low-dimensional F_2-subspace of F_{2^n}' is exactly the Weil-descent factor base, and these are upper bounds on how many such points (and how many solutions of S_{m+1} with all x_i in the subspace) can exist. Bears on the 'variance of yield' and 'coverage' freedoms left open by the summation-cover closure, not on lattice reach.
papers.suggested_route: Read the theorems for the case of an elliptic (or Semaev) curve and a subspace of dimension ell; compare with the measured relation counts at n = 13-45 to see whether the bound is tight (if far from tight, the measured counts carry no structural information; if tight, the subspace cannot be enlarged without changing the count law).

papers.title: Ideal forms of Coppersmith's theorem and Guruswami-Sudan list decoding
papers.authors: Henry Cohn, Nadia Heninger
papers.venue: arXiv 1008.1284 (v2 2013); Advances in Mathematics of Communications 9 (2015)
papers.date: 2010-08-06 (v2 2013-06-25); outside the 2023-2026 window, included as the structural source for T3
papers.summary: Coppersmith's method over polynomial rings, number fields and function fields. Theorem 1.2 (rigorous): for monic f in F[z][x] of degree d modulo p(z) of degree n, all w(z) with deg w < beta^2 n/d and deg gcd(f(w), p) >= beta n are found in polynomial time; equals Guruswami-Sudan when p splits. Lattice reduction over F_q[t] is exact and polynomial-time (Lenstra); multivariate versions correspond to Parvaresh-Vardy / Guruswami-Rudra list decoding.
papers.relevance: T3: on F_{2^n} = F_2[t]/(f) the factor base {deg_t x < ell} is literally the small-root set, so S_{m+1} membership is a function-field Coppersmith problem with exact reduction and (univariate) rigour. delta-reach in units ell/n for S_{m+1}: box-JM 1/(m(m+1)2^{m-2}) (1/24 at m=3, 1/80 at m=4), charging ceiling 1/(m 2^{m-1}) (1/12, 1/32), against the needed ell/n ~ 1/m (1/3, 1/4): the same 8-20x shortfall as over F_p. Novelty of the combination with summation polynomials: novelty_unverified (two targeted searches found nothing).
papers.suggested_route: Toy: n = 31..61, m = 2, build the F_2[t]-lattice for S_3(x1,x2,z) mod f with deg x_i < ell, reduce exactly (Popov/weak-Popov form in python/PARI), check the degree analogue of Howgrave-Graham; expect success iff ell/n <= 1/6 (JM) and failure above 1/4, giving a rigorous certificate that the lattice substitute for Gröbner descent has the same exponent wall.

papers.title: Two variable polynomial congruences and capacity theory
papers.authors: Ted Chinburg, Brett Hemenway Falk, Nadia Heninger, Zachary Scherr
papers.date: 2021-11-28; outside the 2023-2026 window, included as the proof route T1
papers.summary: Second paper relating Coppersmith's method to adelic capacity theory, now for two-variable linear congruences x + t y + a = 0 mod J (HNP, RLWE as special cases). Theorem 1.4: one linear auxiliary function g1 always exists (Minkowski); a computable dichotomy decides whether (1) a second auxiliary polynomial with finite common zero locus exists (method succeeds, finitely many small solutions) or (2) every auxiliary polynomial of ANY degree is divisible by g1 (infinitely many small solutions; Coppersmith's method cannot work). Theorem 3.8: both regimes occur for positive proportions of parameters at X = Y = c sqrt p. Theorems 4.1/1.5: at most one solution when a capacity is small; a small solution of a homogeneous congruence excludes uniformly smaller ones.
papers.relevance: The only framework that bounds ALL auxiliary-polynomial Coppersmith methods, not just a shift-polynomial family; it is the route to turn the W10 1/32 ceiling (full-rank triangular lattices only) into a strategy-independent theorem for S_5, or to show the 'alternative (1)' regime exists for some delta in (1/80, 1/4). The atlas holds only the univariate paper (KN-LIT-3299). S_5 delta-reach: not computed; the counting barrier 1/4 is the only unconditional bound now.
papers.suggested_route: T1 toy: compute the adelic capacity of E = {|x1|,|x2| <= p^delta} x {S_3 = 0 mod p} for S_3 at p ~ 2^20-2^40 (Cantor/Rumely capacity of the archimedean box times the p-adic set) and locate the delta where capacity crosses 1; compare with the measured HG reach 0.10-0.12 and the box limit 1/6; if the crossing is at 1/4 the ceiling is tight for every auxiliary-polynomial method.

papers.title: Solving the Hidden Number Problem for CSIDH and CSURF via Automated Coppersmith
papers.authors: Jonas Meers, Julian Nowakowski
papers.summary: Combinatorial restatement of Coppersmith's method that selects monomials first and then builds polynomials, automating multivariate systems (generalising Jochemsz-May to systems); Sage implementation; CI-HNP solved with ~54% (CSIDH) / ~76% (CSURF) of MSBs.
papers.relevance: Root of the automated line (Ryan, Feng et al., Ding et al.). Already KN-LIT-6744 and in W10's family F (every monomial-set choice MN can make is inside F, hence <= 1/80 asymptotically and <= 1/32 at any ell for S_5).
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: The Hidden Number Problem with Small Unknown Multipliers: Cryptanalyzing MEGA in Six Queries and Other Applications
papers.authors: Keegan Ryan, Nadia Heninger
papers.summary: Formulates HNP with small unknown multipliers (relations a_i alpha ≡ b_i + e_i with unknown small a_i) and a lattice solving it; six-login MEGA key recovery; improved implicit factorisation (May-Ritzenhofen).
papers.relevance: The brief's 'hidden number problem with small unknowns' item. Obstruction for ECDLP: HNP-SUM needs relations LINEAR in the hidden number with small unknown coefficients; in E(F_p) coordinates every relation among x-coordinates of group-related points is Semaev (degree 2^{m-1} per variable) or a division polynomial (degree k^2), never linear, so the lattice shape does not transfer. Already KN-LIT-6993.
papers.suggested_route: None.

papers.title: Improving Bounds on Elliptic Curve Hidden Number Problem for ECDH Key Exchange (and JoC 2026 'New Results on Elliptic Curve Hidden Number Problem for ECDH Key Exchange')
papers.authors: Jun Xu, Santanu Sarkar, Huaxiong Wang, Lei Hu
papers.venue: IACR ePrint 2022/1239; ASIACRYPT 2022; journal version J. Cryptology 2026 (s00145-026-09577-6)
papers.summary: Coppersmith lattices for EC-HNP: recover the hidden ECDH point from partial MSBs of x(P + [i]Q)-type samples; heuristic bound beating both the rigorous 5/6 and heuristic 1/2 fractions for d > 1. JoC 2026 version appears to extend it (snippet: 'for a sufficiently large prime p and a fixed curve'); 2026/1027 reports a further improved EC-HNP bound.
papers.relevance: The EC-HNP equations are low degree because one summand is KNOWN and the unknown is a shift of a known point; the S_5 gate has four unknowns of equal status and degree 8 each. Shows precisely where the elliptic addition law is lattice-friendly (one unknown, partial knowledge) and where it is not (four unknowns, full x). Atlas has KN-LIT-4450.
papers.suggested_route: None for S_5; relevant only to leakage-conversion leads (LEAD-EXO-hnp-advice-leakage).

papers.title: Solving Modular Cubic Equations with Coppersmith's Method
papers.authors: Virgile Dossou-Yovo, Abderrahmane Nitaj, Alain Togbé
papers.summary: UNVERIFIED (publisher page 403; only listing-level description read): Coppersmith's method for small solutions of modular cubic (elliptic-type) equations; a search snippet reports success when the product of the coordinate bounds is below the modulus (for y^2 = x^3 + a x + b mod N the companion Springer 2022 chapter 'Finding Points on Elliptic Curves with Coppersmith's Method' states |x0|^3 |y0|^2 < N, also snippet-level).
papers.relevance: The W10 §7 class 'adding the curve equations y_i^2 = x_i^3 + a x_i + b' is priced by this kind of result: a single curve equation buys nothing when y_i is unconstrained (|y| ~ p), so appending curve equations to the S_5 lattice adds full-size unknowns and cannot raise delta. No S_5 reach change.
papers.suggested_route: None unless y-coordinates are also windowed (then the base shrinks by another p^{1-delta_y} and the yield loss dominates).

papers.title: The Structured Generic-Group Model
papers.authors: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs, Alexandra Henzinger, David J. Wu
papers.summary: Extends Shoup's GGM to algorithms exploiting non-generic structure of a delta-fraction of group elements (precisely defined); any such DL algorithm in a prime-order group runs in time Omega(min(sqrt q, 1/delta)); tight subexponential lower bound for index-calculus-style algorithms exploiting smoothness but otherwise generic.
papers.relevance: Cross-lane but decisive for this lane's accounting: a small-x factor base of B points is structure on a delta = B/p fraction, so an algorithm that is generic outside the base needs time >= min(sqrt p, p/B) = sqrt p whenever B < sqrt p. A lattice S_5 oracle escapes only if it is 'non-generic' on ALL elements (it is: it reads x(R) for arbitrary R), which is the formal statement of the brief's 'field-representation door'. Already KN-LIT-7606 and cited by LEAD-ICE-generic-oracle-arity-cost-floor.
papers.suggested_route: Use its definition to state exactly which step of any proposed lattice oracle is non-generic on non-base elements.

papers.title: Fast Practical Lattice Reduction through Iterated Compression (flatter)
papers.authors: Keegan Ryan, Nadia Heninger
papers.summary: Recursive lattice reduction with iterated precision compression, heuristic O(n^ω (C+n)^{1+ε}); 8192-dimension records; now in PARI/GP and the backend of cuso.
papers.relevance: Engineering; already KN-LIT-3810. Superseded in instruction count by 2026/2541. No reach change.
papers.suggested_route: None.
